target.title: fix(mac): keep launch-at-login app running
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users launching the macOS app at login could have the app unload itself during startup when the launch-at-login toggle hydrated from launchd state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app now refreshes the persisted launch-agent plist while treating an already-loaded job as active state, skipping only the destructive bootout/bootstrap cycle. The loaded-state check queries launchd independently from plist presence, preserving the normal off/on toggle path.

## User Impact

The macOS app remains running after launch-at-login startup instead of disappearing and leaving its login job unloaded.

## Evidence

- Before: bootstrapping `ai.openclaw.mac` launched the app, which rewrote its plist, booted itself out, exited, and left no loaded job.
- After: a signed release app launched from the same agent remained `state = running` with one OpenClaw process and the plist still present after startup hydration.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter LaunchAgentManagerTests` — 7 tests passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
